glosses: to sink or get stuck in something soft
to get stuck (to stay somewhere because obstacles block one from moving on)
to flounder, to get stuck (to become involved in difficulties which prevent one from continuing to work or act)
pogrążać się, zagłębiać się w czymś grząskim, zapadać się

examples.text: Ciężkie wozy grzęzły po osie w błotnistej mazi.

glosses: To become stuck (as if in a bog) and unable to progress.

examples.text: The play bogs down in narrative as we watch Max and Rudy flee Berlin.

DB wanted to start running in 2013, but couldn't get approval for the Velaro trains it wanted to run. It became bogged down in a process controlled by the Intergovernmental Commission (IGC), which includes the Channel Tunnel Safety Authority.

glosses: To cause to become stuck and unable to progress.
